newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ MCI more than 100 bp below RBNZ's preferred mix.
newsitem.headline: NZ MCI more than 100 bp below RBNZ's preferred mix.

text.p: New Zealand's Monetary Conditions Index (MCI) fell to 102 basis points equivalent in interest rate terms below the Reserve Bank's March assumptions on Tuesday.
The MCI measures the degree of variance in money and foreign exchange market conditions from the RBNZ's preferred mix of 90-day rates at 7.5 percent and the Trade-Weighted Index at 68.0.

With a 90-day rate at 7.10 percent and the TWI at 67.13, monetary conditions are very easy, with the MCI standing at -1.04 at 11.53 a.m. (2353 GMT), and financial markets are wary of a Reserve bank comment.
Forex dealers said some in the market believed the bank would comment if the MCI remained at more than 100 basis points below the bank's preferred line for a sustained period of time.
